articleTitle: Design of Double Stator Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor With Low Speed Large Torque
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The permanent magnet synchronous motor with low speed large torque usually has a large volume, and the utilization of the internal space of the rotor of the motor is insufficient. The adoption of double stator topology can make a full use of that internal space, which can improve the power and torque of the motor with double stator topology comparing with the single stator motor of the same size. However, there are not enough researches on this kind of motor, and there are no certain design methods for this type of motor. This paper studies the design method for this kind of motor, including the selection of topological structure, electromagnetic parameters and structural parameters of the motor, and designs a 600kW, 60r/min double stator permanent magnet synchronous motor with low speed large torque. The finite element method was used to analyze the electromagnetic performance of the designed motor. Simulation results show that the designed motor has good no-load characteristics.

articleTitle: Efficiency Optimization Control of IPMSM Considering Varying Machine Parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In order to further improve the efficiency of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) drive, this paper has proposed a simple and effective efficiency optimization control (EOC) strategy for interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs), which is based on the loss model and has considered the compensation of varying machine parameters, such as inductance and equivalent circuit resistance. Simulation results show that this method can achieve a higher efficiency compared with the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control which has also considered the variation of machine parameters.

articleTitle: Mechanical Response Before and After Rotor Inter-turn Short-circuit Fault on Stator Windings in Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper studies on the stator winding electromagnetic force (EF) and mechanical response under rotor interturn short circuit (RISC) fault in synchronous generators. Taking the phase A of stator winding in MJF-30-6 type fault simulating generator as studying object, Firstly, qualitative formulas of the EF before and after RISC are obtained to show the impact of RISC on the harmonic component changes caused by the fault, respectively. Then, 3D finite element calculations are taken to obtain the quantitative EF data for the windings. Finally, solution results based on EF properties, mechanical response before and after RISC on stator winding can be substantiated. It shows that the occurrence of RISC will bring in extra odd harmonics to the EF. Moreover, as RISC takes place, the DC component and (4m-2)-th harmonics (2nd) of the EF will be decreased, while the amplitude of the odd harmonics (1st, 3rd) will be increased. What's more, No matter in normal condition or under RISC, the nose-top, the middle of the involute part, and the connection district between the end winding and the line winding, are the three dangerous positions where the insulation may damaged after a long performance and therefore need special manufacturing and monitoring attention.

articleTitle: An Improvement of Core Losses Estimation Model in Power Electronic Transformer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The accurate estimation of the core loss is significant for the optimal design of the power electronic transformer. This paper proposes an eddy-current loss formula for the solid ferrite with a rectangular cross-sectional area which is widely employed as the high-frequency transformer core, and induces a variable coefficient into the excess loss calculation. The parameters in the excess loss estimation model under the non-sinusoidal voltage excitation are identified based on an experimental tester. The proposed loss model is verified with experimental results and the results show it is feasible to apply this model to the design of a power electronic transformer.

articleTitle: A Novel Algorithm for SOC using Simple Iteration and Coulomb Counting Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Model-based state of charge (SOC) estimation algorithms for batteries have been researched in depth, and the accuracy can be guaranteed. However, as many technologies are fused to enhance the robustness and accuracy of SOC estimation, the huge calculation burden is inevitable. In this paper, a novel model-based SOC estimation algorithm with high accuracy and much lower calculation burden is proposed. Different from existing model-based algorithms such as extend kalman filter and H-infinite filter to estimate SOC, the numerical iterative method is introduced in the proposed algorithm. In comparison, the novel algorithm can reduce more than 90% calculation burden while keeping a high SOC accuracy.

articleTitle: An Accurate and Fast PM Eddy Current Loss Calculation Method for Flux Switching Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the accurate and fast permanent magnet (PM) eddy current loss calculation method for flux switching permanent magnet (FSPM) machine. First, the 3D finite element analysis (FEA) model is used and the distributions of the magnetic vector potential (MVP) and eddy current loop are presented, based on which a modified combining 2D FEA electromagnetic computation and analytical equations is proposed to calculate PM eddy current loss. Then the axial and radial segmentation of magnets are taken into consideration. The results obtained by the proposed method is proved to be extremely close to those obtained by 3D FEA.

articleTitle: An Advanced Speed Control Scheme for the High Speed Blender Machine using BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a variable reference speed control of a high-speed Brushless DC(BLDC) motor for blender machines is proposed for reducing the speed ripple at the high-speed pulsating load variation condition. A high-speed 2-pole BLDC motor is designed to satisfy the operating speed and the efficiency of the blender machine. According to the pulsating load, the motor speed is pulsated by the conventional current limit control scheme in the constant power region. In order to improve the grinding performance, the reference speed is automatically varied to overcome the pulsating load variation in the proposed method. From the reference speed control, the output torque of the motor can satisfy the pulsating load of the blender machine. The designed high speed BLDC motor and the proposed control scheme are verified by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: MTPA Control of IPMSM with Aiding from Estimation of dq-axis Inductances
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control scheme for interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) considering inductance variation. It utilizes Ferrari's method to get a minimum current vector for a given torque command. It also identifies the dq-axis inductances of IPMSM by model reference adaptive system (MRAS) based on the Popov stability criterion, which could aid the real-time calculation of optimal current vector. This method does not need to know inductance values or premade lookup table in advance. What's more, it has a good robustness against the variation of inductance. The performance of the proposed control method is finally verified in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Full-order ESO Based Disturbance Rejection Method With a Simple Parameter Tuning for Electro-Mechanical Servo System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In order to improve the disturbance rejection performance of electro-mechanical actuator (EMA), a robust servo system based on full-order extended state observer (ESO) is proposed for EMA employing permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Firstly, dynamic model of EMA is analyzed. Parameter uncertainties and load variation are treated as total disturbances. Utilizing this model, a parallel composite control of position and speed with command shaping is presented to improve the frequency bandwidth of EMA. Secondly, a full-order ESO is designed to estimate total disturbances. Thirdly, a simple parameter tuning method is given, which is convenient to analyze and implement the controller. The disturbance sensitivity analysis is realized in frequency domain. Finally, the simulation and experimental results verify the effectiveness of proposed strategy for EMA.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Switched Reluctance Motor Based on Response Surface Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Switched reluctance motor (SRM) has been applied in more and more fields. However, the larger torque ripple and lower power density limit its filed. The response surface model (RSM) of optimizing parameters of motor structure is built based on the analysis of the causes of motor torque ripple in order to reduce the vibration and noise of the motor. The multi-group sample points are constructed by using the central composite design (CCD) method, where the torque ripple and efficiency are taken as the optimization objective, and the stator pole, rotor pole arc and turn-off angle are the optimization variables. The sample data are obtained by finite element analysis (FEA), and the RSM equation is built. The effect of all factors on the response face value is analyzed. The relationship between the variables and the target is determined by studying the interaction between the stator/rotor pole arcs and the outer diameter of the rotor. According to the verification formula of response surface, the complex correlation coefficient of torque ripple and efficiency are 0.929 and 0.962; and the lack of fit are 0.059 and 0.056 respectively, which show that the linear relationship is significant between response surface and independent variables. The simulation results show that the torque ripple, average torque and efficiency are 0.608,4.558 and 0.827 when the stator pole arc, rotor pole arc and turn-off angle is 19 deg., 24.4 deg., 22 deg., respectively.

articleTitle: Measurement of Proximity Losses in Litz Wires
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a method to measure the proximity losses of the Litz wire. A test bench is built to produce uniform alternating magnetic field in two air gaps. When the Litz wire are put into the air gaps, the proximity losses of the Litz wire are produced, and can be measured. Furthermore, the field density can be measured by a detecting coil. Then the curve of proximity losses versus field density can be finally obtained.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on An Improved Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a sensorless speed control method for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) based on an improved sensorless sliding mode observer vector control algorithm with dynamic boundary layer, suitable for applications in medium-high speed. Compared with conventional SMO, the signum function is replaced by a saturation function, to reduce the chattering problem. Also, in order to compensate for the position error caused by the low-pass filter, this control method allows the boundary layer to change with speed, making the rotor speed and position estimation more accurate in a wide speed range. The validity of the proposed sensorless velocity control method has been demonstrated with real experiments.

articleTitle: Direct Control of Bearingless Permanent Magnet Slice Motor Based on Stator Flux Observer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The theory and method of direct torque control are applied to the torque and suspension force control of the bearingless permanent magnet slice motor (BPMSM) in this paper. Meanwhile, aiming at the defects of low precision and result lag of flux linkage observation, a novel stator flux observer combining the phase-locked loop (PLL) and prediction control module is introduced. Firstly, the operating principle of the BPMSM is analyzed, and the mathematical models are set up. Secondly, the PLL flux linkage observer is designed, then the prediction control models and direct control algorithm are given. Thirdly, the direct control system of the BPMSM is constructed by Matlab/Simulink. Finally, the feasibility and correctness of the flux linkage observer and control algorithm are verified through simulation and experiment. The research results show that the disturbance recovery time is shortened by 35 ms and the vibration amplitude and regulation time of the rotor are significantly reduced by around 39% and 40%, respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Rotor Eddy Current Loss in High-Speed PM Brushless DC Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes an experimental method for measuring the rotor eddy current loss in high-speed PM brushless DC motors. The principle of the method is to measure the loss when the rotor is stationary and the corresponding current harmonics are applied to the stator. The eddy current losses of the rotors with various types of retaining sleeve structures are measured and compared, and thus the validation of the experimental method is verified. Furthermore, the influences of rotor retaining sleeve structures, including stainless steel sleeve, non-conductive sleeve and laminated sleeve, with and without copper layer, on the rotor eddy current loss in a high-speed PM brushless DC motor have been comprehensively investigated.

articleTitle: Design and Economical Evaluation of Small-Capacity Motor Used in Household Appliances by Taguchi Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper presents design and optimization methodology of a permanent magnet brushless DC motor (BLDC), with 25 W rated at 1,800 rpm, by Taguchi method to optimize efficiency and performance of electric fan motors. With optimization algorithm, we proposed the optimal structure of permanent magnet dimensions and stator tooth size. Due to the nonlinear characteristics of ferromagnetic materials, analysis and design are manipulated with finite element method (FEM). Finally, the proposed motor structure and simulation results are verified with conventional induction motors via FEM.

articleTitle: Study on LVRT of DFIG Wind Power System Based on Crowbar Protection Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The wind power system based on the Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) is one of the most popular wind power systems considering the economy and performance. However, DFIG is extremely sensitive to the grid fluctuations or faults since its stator side connected directly to the grid. When the grid voltage drops heavily, hardware protection must be required to ensure the system ride through the low voltage stage. The Crowbar Protection Circuit (CPC) is most popularly used. This paper studies the transient process of the system when the grid voltage drops. And then, the crowbar resistance and the best CPC duration are optimized by the analytic expression of transient current on the rotor side based on the standard of Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT). The results show that the optimal crowbar resistance and the right time to remove the CPC are relevant to the rotor current transient component and the time constant. Finally, the feasibility by using grid-side converter as a STATCOM to support the reactive power of the grid during the stage of crowbar protection is discussed. The results are simulated by MATLAB/Simulink and verifies the correctness of the theory analysis.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Water Cooling System for High Power Density Permanent Magnet Motor Based on Multi-physics Field Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Since the high power density permanent magnet motor has the characteristics of large unit volume loss and heat generation, this paper proposes a design and optimization method for the cooling system of this type of motor, and takes a 48-slot 40-pole high power density permanent magnet motor as an example. Firstly, various losses of the prototype are calculated with finite-element method, especially winding copper loss and permanent magnet eddy current loss. Then, based on the heat transfer theory, equivalent models of stator windings and air gap are introduced to establish the 3-D temperature field model. Finally, in order to improve the prototype's heat dissipation capability, the water cooling system is designed and optimized. The design results are verified by multi-physics field simulation, which provides references for the design of the water cooling system of the high power density permanent magnet motor.

articleTitle: Predictive Control of Surface PMSM Direct Torque Control System using Voltage Vectors with Variable Angle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Based on flux and torque’s expressions of surface permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) direct torque control (DTC) system, values of stator flux and torque at next sampling point after applying voltage vector with different angle are given in this paper. The objective function is proposed which aims to minimize stator flux and torque’s error. The predictive control will select the optimal angle corresponding to the minimum objective function. Simulation results show the surface PMSM DTC system under the predictive control works properly. The predictive control selects the optimal voltage vector from aggregate of voltage vectors with different angle. More selectable voltage vectors will lead to better control performance, but it will cause heavier calculation burden. In this paper, control performances of surface PMSM DTC system using different aggregates of voltage vectors are studied. Considering control performance and calculation burden, an ideal aggregate of voltage vector is given.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Loss of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is introduced to optimize the multi-objective of permanent magnet synchronous motor, reduce loss and improve efficiency. In order to reduce the loss of the permanent magnet synchronous motor, the four main parameters that affect the loss (magnetic pole thickness, air gap length, slot width, groove depth,) are optimized. By using orthogonal experiment to select a certain number of samples, using support vector machine (SVM) to fitting the data to get the regression equation, using particle swarm optimization algorithm to optimize the regression equation, get the optimal solution, Maxwell model in ANSYS simulation analysis into the motor. The simulation results show that the loss reduction and efficiency of PMSM are improved by 2.64% compared with that before optimization.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Commutation Leading Angle Control of Static Frequency Converter for the Startup of Large-scale Synchronous Condenser
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Static frequency converter is widely used in startup of large-scale synchronous condensers. In high-speed stage, the inverter on the machine side adopts natural commutation, and the commutation leading angle β is usually set 60°. However, it restrains quick startup. In this paper, a control method of commutation leading angle β is proposed to reduce the startup time. For control of β, the arc extinguishing angle γ, the load angle δ , and the thyristor commutation overlap angle μ are calculated. According to the simulation result of startup in Matlab/Simulink, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Investigation on Slot and Pole Combination Schemes for Six-phase Fault-Tolerant Permanent Magnet Rim Driven Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In order to improve the reliability of marine electric propulsion system, the topology of fault-tolerant permanent magnet rim driven motor is proposed. The slot and pole combination and winding distribution of six-phase fault-tolerant permanent magnet rim driven motor are theoretically analyzed. Besides, the general design method is given. The simulation results of finite element analysis is provided to verify the short-circuit current suppression capability and mutual inductance reduction method in different case of slot and pole combination, which provides a reference for the application of fault-tolerant permanent magnet rim driven motor in ship propulsion field.

articleTitle: Equivalent Magnetic Circuit Analysis for Linear Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The paper proposes a novel linear transverse flux permanent magnet machine with the flux-concentrating of three side wall in the mover which has the characteristics of high force density and high reliability. Firstly, the novel structure and work principle of the linear TFPM machine are introduced. Secondly, the equivalent magnetic circuit model is established by analyzing the magnetic flux distribution between the relative positions with stator and mover. Thirdly, the results of magnetic network model are calculated by the first law of Kirchhoff magnetic circuit, and are compared with the three-dimensional finite element model. Finally, a prototype is constructed and experiments show good agreement with the finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Research on EBE-FEM Realized by CUDA Applying to Electromagnetic Field Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The utilization of Graphical Processing Units (GPUs) for element by element (EBE) finite element method (FEM) is demonstrated in this paper. Different from the conventional FEM, the iterative solution scheme of EBE can be entirely decomposed into computations on the element level without assembling the global system matrix, and the computations can be executed parallel. GPUs are programmable stream processors designed for intensive, highly parallelized computations, and the many-core nature can support computation element by element in parallel. In this paper, the EBE-FEM combined with Jacobi preconditioned technology is derived. The CPU+GPU cooperative computation model of EBE finite element method based on Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) platform is proposed. The corresponding FEM program are developed and implemented on the magnetic field calculations which produced by straight conductor carrying current and single phase power transformer respectively. The validity and accuracy of the method have been verified by comparing the result with the analytical solution. Compared with the serial EBE-FEM, the higher computational efficiency can be obtained by parallel EBE computation on CUDA. The proposed method can be applied to electromagnetic field analysis of transformer and motor, which may refer large scale numerical computation.

articleTitle: An impact of influence of power system operating condition over different type of PSS in a SMIB
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Low frequency oscillations in power systems are one of the major barriers to improve the dynamic performance of power systems. To ensure the effectiveness of these stabilizers the design of stabilizer should be robust over a wide range of power system operation conditions. In this paper, the comparison of three different stabilizers (PSS, BESS active power and BESS reactive power) is presented using Eigen value analysis in an SMIB. All stabilizers employ phase compensation method for parameter designs. The effectiveness of these stabilizers is demonstrated through a non-linear time domain simulation over a wide range of power system operating conditions that influences the parameter of transmission line. The simulation study shows that at light loading both BESS base active and reactive power stabilizers are least effective as compared to PSS. However, as the power system operating condition changes only BESS active power stabilizer provides robustness. Its Eigen value doesn’t show a significant change. It was found that BESS reactive power is more effective when it operates at higher operating conditions. It provides more damping to power system which helps to suppress low frequency oscillations effectively. In contrast, the performance of PSS decreases with increase in the loading, it provides less damping at higher loadings. Moreover, BESS active and reactive power stabilizers were found to be more effective as length of transmission line increase while PSS effectiveness decreases with increase in length of transmission line.

articleTitle: Comparison between Conventional and Novel Self-excited Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper investigates a novel multi-phase self-excited synchronous machine, which can provide high torque at zero or very low speed. The introduced machine utilizes independent multi-phase stator winding generates the rotor excitation. The rotor contains two winding sets, and a multiphase diode rectifier connected between them. Compared with conventional solutions, higher torque capability at zero speed can be achieved. Furthermore, the steady-state and dynamic performance are verified via simulation results.

articleTitle: Suppression of Low-Frequency Oscillation with Cascaded H-bridge Multi-level Active Power Filter in Vehicle-Grid System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In recent years, The low-frequency instability phenomenon frequently occurs in the vehicle-grid system of high-speed railway when multiple units (EMUs) operate in one railway station simultaneously, which leads to the traction blockade of EMUs and directly influences the normal operation of high-speed railway system. To solve this problem, a single-phase cascaded H-bridge multi-level active power filter (APF) directly connected to the 27.5kV traction network is proposed, which can operate in two different modes. In mode 1, APF is only utilized for inter-harmonic compensation, while in mode 2, APF is utilized for inter-harmonic and reactive compensation. To verify the suppression effect of APF on the low-frequency oscillation (LFO), some time-domain simulations in MATLAB are implemented. The simulation results show that the APF can suppress the LFO effectively in both modes. Moreover, it is also verified that the change of system parameters have little impact on the performance of APF.

articleTitle: Improvement of Steinmetz’s Parameters Fitting Formula for Ferrite Soft Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The Steinmetz's parameters are essential for calculation of the losses in soft magnetic materials. However, due to the non-uniform flux density distribution in the soft magnetic material cores, the fitting error of the original Steinmetz equation (OSE) is considerable. This paper investigates the fitting method of the Steinmetz's parameters, and an improved formula is proposed to minimize the influence of the non-uniform distribution of flux density. Experimental results show that the error is reduced dramatically using the proposed fitting method and improved formula.

articleTitle: Impacts of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine under Different Rotor Temperature
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Along with the development of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM), the variation of rotor temperature has become the main restriction of Electrical Vehicle (EV) motor design. In this paper, we mainly investigated the relationship between temperature and performance of the motor (output torque, efficiency map, etc.). Simulating results and analysis are given based on the CAE software ANSOFT, using a specific PMSM model equipped with Permanent Magnet (PM) with the grade N38UH. Several conclusions are given to provide a new perspective in motor R&D process, by adding the consideration of relationship between temperature and performance while remaining undemagnetized in normal working condition.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characteristics Analysis of High Speed Generator with Permanent Magnet Layered Bundling Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The high-speed permanent magnet generator (HSPMG) has the advantages of high power density, small volume, etc. It does not need a gear speed increase box to connect directly to high-speed load or a prime mover, thus overcoming many problems such as high failure rate and difficult maintenance of the conventional generator system. HSPMG has obtained more and more extensive applications in many fields. Aiming at the problem that permanent magnets for high-speed permanent magnet generator damage due to high centrifugal force under high-speed rotation and excessive eddy current loss on the rotor surface, this paper proposes a new type of permanent magnet rotor structure with layered lashing. This paper analyzes a 350kW, 30000r/min new rotor of HSPMG and determines the relevant parameters of the generator. The finite element method (FEM) is used to analyze the new rotor of HSPMG with different permanent magnet layers from three aspects of no-load characteristics, rotor surface eddy current loss and rotor strength to get the optimal solution.

articleTitle: Predictive Control with Variable Amplitude of Voltage Vector of Surface PMSM Direct Torque Control System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Based on flux and torque’s expressions of surface permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) direct torque control (DTC) system, the values of stator flux and torque at next sampling point after applying voltage vector with different amplitude are given in this paper. And objective function of flux and torque’s error is proposed which only uses the amplitude of applying voltage vector as the variable. The predictive control will select the optimal voltage vector which aims to minimize objective function. Simulation results show the PMSM DTC system under the control of proposed strategy works properly. The predictive control selects the optimal voltage vector from aggregate of voltage vectors. More selectable voltage vectors will lead to better control performance, but it will cause heavier calculation burden. In this paper, control performances of surface PMSM DTC system are given using 9 aggregates of selectable voltage vectors. Considering control performance and calculation burden, dividing voltage vector into three equal parts to get 3 selectable voltage vectors is an ideal way.

articleTitle: A Novel Concept of Pseudo Harmonic Transmission Ratio in PM Vernier Motor for In-Wheel Traction Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes the novel concept titled as pseudo harmonic transmission ratio (PHTR) in permanent magnet vernier motor (PMVM) for in-wheel traction. The PHTR is equivalent to the mechanical gear in conventional transmission. Hence, the torque expressions of PMVM and PMSM plus mechanical gear are both derived and analyzed by theoretical analysis and FEA respectively. Moreover, the output capability of PMVM with same PHTR is compared with the PMSM plus mechanical reduction gear under the same in-wheel space. Meanwhile, in order to evaluate the harmonic discount degree comparing with the mechanical reduction gear, the harmonic transmission factor k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">htf</sub> is introduced and defined in PMVM, which will contribute to further understanding the harmonic working principle. Finally, the results between theoretical analysis and FEA method match well, which exactly validates the accuracy of results.

articleTitle: Accurate Equivalent Circuit Modeling and Identification of Solid rotor Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In view of the short comings of traditional synchronous machine transient model, in this paper, an accurate equivalent circuit modeling and parameter identification method is proposed. In this new modeling method, the phenomenon of unequal mutual reactance of different windings and the eddy current during transient process on solid rotor are taken into consideration and thus derive a model that better reflects the actual physic phenomenon inside the motor. Then, dynamic parameters of this accurate model are identified using a DC step signal test. In this process, a chaotic simulated annealing particle swarm algorithm is used to obtain the values of dynamic parameters. Finally, the presented method in this paper is applied on a 300 MVA solid rotor synchronous machine and validated by finite element analysis.

Author Keywords: chaotic simulated annealing particle swarm algorithm

articleTitle: Research on fault-tolerant control method for demagnetization faults of permanent magnet synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the loss of magnetic field of permanent magnet synchronous motor causes the performance of motor with load to decline, a fault-tolerant control method based on adaptive observer flux linkage on-line detection is proposed. Firstly, according to the predictive control model of permanent magnet synchronous motor, the influence of loss of magnetic field on current control and motor running state is analyzed. Secondly, the adaptive observer is used to accurately observe the flux linkage, and then the observed value of the state current is obtained. Finally, the observed value of the state current is fed back to the controller so that the response current can accurately track the given current, thus realizing the stable operation of the motor. Simulation results show that the method is feasible.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Low-Cost High-Speed Switched Reluctance Motor for Supercharger
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the design, optimization, and analysis of a low-cost high-speed 4/2 poles switched reluctance motor (SRM) for electric supercharger (ESC) are presented. The proposed motor simply consists of only cores with ferromagnetic material lamination and concentrated windings on the stator. First, the core material is selected and stator geometry is optimized by implementing Genetic Algorithm (GA) to reduce radial force which may lead to reduced vibration and noise during operation. Then, the electrical characteristics of the motor are examined with finite element analysis (FEA). In order to further reduce the cost, a simple hall-effect sensor is used to excite the phase. Dynamic analysis shows the viability of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Drive Control of PMSM Considering Nonlinear Modeling Error in Over-modulation Region
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a single-mode overmodulation algorithm based on space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) is introduced. The nonlinear modeling error in the conventional single-mode overmodulation region has been investigated and an improvement is consequently proposed. Which uses the Fourier series expansion to achieve a precise linear and accurate control of the reference voltage and the fundamental component of inverter output voltage. The proposed method is then investigated on a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) drive control system modeled in Matlab/Simulink and shows better accuracy in voltage control.

articleTitle: Composite control of speed sensorless for bearingless permanent magnet synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: It is difficult to achieve precise estimation of rotor position for a bearingless permanent magnet synchronous motor(BPMSM) with a single position sensorless control method in different speed range. In order to solve this problem, a composite control strategy combining an improved pulsating high frequency signal injection and second order generalized integrator frequency-locked phase-locked loop(SOGI-FLL-PLL) method is proposed. Firstly, the structure and working principle of the BPMSM are introduced. Secondly, the principle of position and speed estimation by high frequency pulsating signal injection method based on SOGI is studied. Thirdly, the method of SOGI-FLL-PLL used in medium and high speed operation is analyzed. In the state of low and medium switching interval, a linear weighted control algorithm is adopted to make the two control strategies transit smoothly. Finally, the simulations and experiments are carried out. The results show that the proposed composite control method can estimate rotor position and speed accurately and the rotor can return to the balance position quickly under the conditions of load disturbance, which validate good effectiveness of composite strategy and good robustness of the whole sensorless control system.

articleTitle: Simulation and experiments on a sparkle model of a current-changing DC generator (DCG)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In order to make the system analysis and research of a certain type ship main converter unit safer and more economical, according to the mathematical model of the main converter unit, the normal working condition and the emergency working condition models of the main converter unit are built based on the MATLAB simulation software. The simulation models are used to analyze the operating conditions of the main converter unit, when the loads are suddenly loading and unloading, the harmonic analysis is performed on the AC voltage by FFT. The simulation results shows that the model can better simulate the operation characteristics of the main converter unit and lay an established foundation for the intensive study of the main converter unit.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Electromagnetic Performance of Multi-Tooth Switching Flux Permanent Magnet Memory Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-tooth switching flux permanent magnet memory (SFPMM) machine is designed and compared with conventional multi-tooth switching flux PM (SFPM) machine in terms of electromagnetic performance. Moreover, the flux adjustment capability and flux weakening capability are also compared between SFPMM machine and conventional SFPM machine. It shows that the novel multi-tooth SFPMM machine has better flux adjustment capability.

articleTitle: Design an Efficiency Assessment of Solar Thermal Updraft Tower with Molten Salt as Heat Storage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This research focuses on improving the solar updraft tower efficiency by including a solar collector with parabolic trays and molten salt as heat storage to the system. The objectives of this research are (1) to design a solar thermal updraft tower with molten salt as heat storage for electricity generation by studying and optimizing its parameters and (2) to assess the efficiency of the system and to compare it with the original design. ANSYS CFX is used to calculate the power output of the system. The first parameter is the tower height to roof radius ratio which ranges between 0.2 - 2.2 while fixing the surface area of solar thermal updraft tower as a constant value. The baseline dimension of the tower is taken from the 50kW Manzanares prototype in Spain. The study shows that electrical power output increases with the tower height to roof radius ratio. Two pipe arrangements, namely a reversed pipe layout and the single pipe layout are studied. It is found that the single pipe layout yields a higher energy output. The single pipe arrangement is then further studied to assess the effect of pipe number with 12, 24, 36, 48 and 60 pipes evenly spaced around the tower in the radial direction. It is found that the system with 36 pipes gives the lowest ratio of oil used to power generated. The results show that solar thermal updraft tower with 36 single pipes generates up to 157.15 kW. The efficiency of the system is 8.93% which is 96 times higher than the original solar thermal updraft tower efficiency of only 0.09%.

articleTitle: Torque Performance Analysis of Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor Based on Rotor Structure Parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The rotor of the permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor is composed of multilayer flux barriers embedded permanent magnets. Due to the complex structure of the rotor, the torque performance of the motor is greatly affected by the structural parameters of the rotor. This paper mainly studies the influences of rotor structural parameters such as flux barrier shape, number of layers, rib width, air gap length and permanent magnet parameters such as permanent magnet width and thickness on torque performance. Then, the torque performance comparison between permanent magnet-assisted reluctance motor and surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor with the same permanent magnet usage is made. The research results show that the length of air gap and the width of rotor ribs are the most important parameters that affect the torque performance of the motor. In addition, adding a small amount of permanent magnets to the magnetic barrier can significantly increase the motor output torque.

Author Keywords: permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor

articleTitle: A Fast Speed Control of PMSMs without Proportional Integral Controller
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motor control system requires fast current response and anti-interference capability. The traditional control method mostly adopts vector control, and proportional-integral (PI) regulator is used in its current inner loop. It is difficult to take into account the rapidity and stability of the response when the parameters are not adjusted properly. The external speed PI regulator is prone to fluctuate greatly when subjected to external disturbances. Deadbeat current predictive control has the characteristics of fast response and constant switching frequency, which is especially suitable for discrete system control. In this paper, the deadbeat predictive control strategy is adopted in the current loop, and the system has a fast dynamic response. In order to enhance the anti-jamming ability of the system, the sliding mode control is used in the speed loop, and the adverse effects caused by the load are well suppressed. Experimental results show that the control strategy presented in this paper has good system response and robustness.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of an Extended Range Generator for EVs Based on Taguchi Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a description and operating principles of a novel hybrid excited synchronous generator are presented for EVs. The excitation source is produced by two permanent magnets of different sizes and field windings. The latter can regulate the magnetic density of air gap and then adjust the output DC voltage and current. The advantage is to match the engine output power with the battery charging characteristics. In addition, several factors are discussed to achieve an optimum output power for an extended range of mileage. Arrangements of armature windings and magnetic poles are investigated for an optimum no-load voltage. The excitation sources including excitation windings and sizes of magnets are calculated according to the excitation voltage and magnetomotive force demand. Taguchi optimized method is adopted to investigate the size of magnets and number of winding turns for the optimum output power. Moreover, electromagnetic finite element analysis(FEA) and thermal analysis of a 30kW extended range synchronous generator are given to verify the design.

articleTitle: Simulation of cross-border capacity allocation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The demand for transfer capacities at the transmission interconnections between Control Areas in Europe is usually much higher than the capacity available for electricity trading. It is expected, that as a consequence of market opening according to the market liberalization in Europe, the demand will further increase over time. The pursue of an Integrated European Electricity Market (IEM) still holds many unsolved challenges for the system operators. To resolve this problem, it is important to have a well-organized transmission capacity auction platform where the market participants can purchase the rights of the transmission capacity. It is also important for these participants to make winning bids on the transmission rights for various amount of energy. This paper focuses on creating a model which is capable of simulating cross-border capacity auctions. After a short description, simulations of a capacity auctions will be presented using various numbers of agents as bidders and another agent as the auctioneer. Then an advanced modelling of transmission capacity auctioning will be presented. Improving the created simulation model with the implementation of two agent-learning methods will be shown. Finally, evaluation of the results and the possibilities of improvement, and the future objectives of this work will be described.

articleTitle: Research on Sensorless BLDCM Control Strategy Based on Line Voltage Difference
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The sensorless control strategy has become one of the important research directions of brushless DC motors. Researchers have proposed a variety of rotor position signal detection methods. Now, brushless DC motor position sensors usually use the back EMF to detect the zero-crossing point. While the zero-crossing point of the back EMF of the non-conducting phase winding is detected, and then delay 30° electrical angle to obtain the commutation time. But the method needs to reconstruct the neutral point of the motor with a certain error. In order to avoid the influence of the error, the paper studies and analyzes the rotor position detection technology based on the line voltage difference based on the traditional back EMF zero-crossing signal detection technology. Finally, a test platform based on STM32F103 development board was built. The feasibility of the method was verified by the actual operation of the motor.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Compatibility of Secondary Circuit of Electronic Voltage Transformer Under the Action of VFTO
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: To analyze the electromagnetic interference caused by VFTO to the electronic voltage transformer, this paper conducts equivalent modeling and simulation analysis in accordance with the generating features of VFTO and structural characteristics of electronic voltage transformer. The simulation model is built in the test condition of opening and closing the bus with the disconnector, to obtain the VFTO simulation waveform. With VFTO signal as the excitation, equivalent circuit is established for the capacitive divider, and capacitive bleeder circuit outputs high frequency transient signals while operating the disconnector, with the output voltage peak reaching 2.8kV at maximum, which makes the signal acquisition unable to work normally. According to the results, while operating the disconnector, VTFO signal incurred may impact the secondary output signal of electronic voltage transformer greatly, and it provides a strong evidence for the research on the electromagnetic protection of electronic voltage transformer.

articleTitle: Real-time Determination of PMSM Assembly Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a temperature observer for the stator winding and rotor permanent magnets of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs). The observer is based on the algorithm of model reference adaptive system (MRAS). The MRAS algorithm based on Popov stability criterion is used to monitor the stator winding resistance and permanent magnet flux linkage of the motor. The observer monitors assembly temperatures based on the fact that the permanent magnet flux linkage and stator winding resistance are temperature-dependent parameters. Simulation results show good performance in temperature tracking.

articleTitle: Strategy Design for Controlling On-Chip Photonic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper does an extensive analysis of high-speed bipolar junction transistor which includes the structure of the transistor and doping concentration of each region. The main limitations of the desired characteristic are parasitic capacitance and carrier recombination regions. The gain of the amplifier will decrease as the operation frequency increase because of the parasitic capacitance. The bipolar junction transistor design is mainly aiming to reduce the parasitic capacitance and ensure that the recombination occurs at collector region. Furthermore, a photonic circuit is introduced in the project. The photonic circuit is unstable because of a susceptible cavity. The circuit can be enhanced by introducing a feedback control circuit. This work will also use the designed BJT to construct a feedback control circuit which includes a differential amplifier and a reference current generator. The feedback control circuit will not only make the photonic circuit stable but also be efficient and low noise. The layout of the full feedback control circuit and the structure of the BJT are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the designed strategy for controlling on-chip photonic circuits.

articleTitle: Analysis of Resilience of Distributed System with Photovoltaic Based on Seismic Damage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: The conventional analysis of reliability of power systems is well established, but for the problem caused by extreme natural disasters, there is of great significance to establish the evaluation method to analyze the ability of the distributed systems to withstand the destruction caused by the extreme natural disasters. Compared with the traditional reliability analysis, the concept of the distributed system resilience indexes (RI) which mainly focus on the highly destructive but rare events is presented in this paper to indicate this kind of ability. Seism is a typical rare event, which has different characteristics of damage to power grid compared to other highly destructive rare events. And the impact on the power grid resilience caused by the distributed photovoltaic (PV) cluster interconnected to the grid is also discussed. After analyzing these characteristics, this paper proposes the RI of distributed systems respectively based on the features of seism and the way of how to calculate it. Finally, an example of a distribution system model is used to verify the validity of the resilience indexes.

articleTitle: An Improved Phase Angle Prediction Method for Quasi-synchronous Grid Connection of Large-scale Synchronous Condenser
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: To enhance the safety of grid connection of large-scale synchronous condenser, an improved method to predict the phase angle is proposed. For high-speed rotating machines, phase angle prediction is prone to be inaccurate with constant leading time. A forecasting method by Taylor series is adopted in this paper to reduce the deviation in phase angle prediction, thus the inrush current of grid connection would be minimized. Simulation is carried out in PSCAD, the method is proved effective.

articleTitle: Voltage Closed-Loop Feedback Control of Hybrid Excited Switching Flux Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: In the hybrid excited switching flux permanent magnet (HESFPM) machine, the d-axis flux linkage can be adjusted by both the armature current and the dc field current. In order to produce high torque within a widen speed range, a voltage closed-loop feedback control strategy is proposed in this paper. The error between the feedback voltage and the maximum phase voltage is used to determine the operation region of flux weakening control and adjust the dc field current and d-axis current in the flux weakening region. The proposed method is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Comparison of different Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet patterns
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: This paper investigates how to improve the compactness of a Synchronous Permanent Magnet Surface Mounted machine for high-frequency and high torque direct-drive applications. For that, the performances such as power mass density and losses of different pole patterns, e.g. Halbach and conventional radial magnetized magnet arrays are compared. Depending on the given specifications, some considerations concerning the decision-making process, taking into account process and assembly constraints when choosing between the conventional radial magnetization and the Halbach array, are reported.

articleTitle: Utilizing Flexibility Services from a Large Heat Pump to Postpone Grid Reinforcement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems
abstract: Distribution grid reinforcement problem is considered in this paper. Annual growth of the electric loads may lead to the congestion situations in the distribution network, where current flowing through components exceed their maximum current carrying capacity (MCCC). A conventional solution is to reinforce overloaded components, i.e. to replace it with the one with higher capacity. However, this will lead to the additional investments for the distribution system operator (DSO). An alternative solution is to utilize flexibility services (FS) such as reconfiguration (RE) and demand response (DR) to provide peak reduction from the large controllable loads (e.g. a heat pump) in the system. Several forecasts of the future load growth simulated in the MATPOWER are used to study the proposed solutions and identify their feasibility. The results show that both FS can be used to defer grid reinforcement providing economic benefits for the DSO.
